triggers: Investigation of an existing workflow and competing implementation approaches
Synthesis across a substantial product brief, protocol, schemas, and operational examples
Creation of substantial design and implementation-planning artifacts
reasoning_heavy_assessment.justification: The task is to convert a product vision and an existing manual protocol into a reliable human-in-the-loop system design, requiring independent architectural judgment, web research, risk analysis, migration planning, and test design.

title: Design the upgraded ChatGPT Web Call Assistant from the existing protocol
objective: Independently analyze the supplied product brief and the current working ChatGPT Web-call protocol, then produce a concrete, implementation-ready design for a user-controlled system that preserves the existing exchange history and reliability principles while adding the proposed Chrome-extension-assisted Go/Done workflow, durable state tracking, validation, recovery, and whole-project completion management.

in_scope: Read every uploaded file completely and reconstruct how the current manual system works end to end.
Distinguish explicit product requirements, current authoritative behavior, examples, assumptions, recommendations, and unresolved choices.
Evaluate at least three feasible implementation architectures and recommend one using an explicit decision matrix.
Design responsibilities and boundaries for Codex, the local orchestration layer, the Chrome extension, ChatGPT Web, the filesystem exchange folders, and the user.

Design the complete Go-to-Done workflow, including preparation, user confirmation, submission, response readiness, collection, validation, revision, acceptance, integration, pause, retry, and failure recovery.
Design a durable state machine and machine-readable data contracts that remain compatible with or deliberately migrate the existing timestamped request/response exchange layout.

Address safe request packaging, exact file disclosure, response-to-call association, download handling, browser/session uncertainty, idempotency, resumability, traceability, logging, privacy, least privilege, and protection against collecting unrelated page content.
Define what can and cannot be reliably automated in a changing ChatGPT Web UI while preserving a clear user-authorized action boundary.

Provide a phased implementation roadmap with verification gates and a comprehensive test strategy, including mocked tests, browser integration tests, failure injection, manual user-acceptance tests, and rollback criteria.
Identify the smallest coherent first implementation slice that proves the architecture without pretending the entire product is complete.
Use current web research where necessary to verify browser-extension platform constraints and relevant ChatGPT/OpenAI product constraints.
out_of_scope: Writing or modifying repository code in this call
Returning a finished Chrome extension or executable implementation
Changing the supplied product requirements, protocol files, schemas, examples, or repository instructions
Using or requesting secrets, credentials, API keys, browser cookies, or authentication exports
Analyzing the thesis or defense content contained incidentally in the operational example beyond understanding the call mechanics
Claiming literal 100 percent reliability in conditions outside the system's control
Designing hidden, unattended, or user-bypassing automation

source_authority.role: Primary product intent and user-experience requirements
allowed_uses: Determine the target product behavior, role boundaries, human-control requirements, reliability ambition, and completion model
Identify requirements that the proposed design must satisfy
prohibited_uses: Treating deliberately unspecified technical choices as already decided
Weakening the explicit user-control and no-hidden-automation requirements

source_authority.role: Authoritative current repository gate and manual Web-call protocol
allowed_uses: Reconstruct current triage, exchange-folder, transport, output, authority, and validation rules
prohibited_uses: Assuming the current manual transport is the required final architecture
Overriding the product brief where the brief explicitly upgrades the system

source_authority.source: WEB_REQUEST_SCHEMA.json, WEB_RESPONSE_SCHEMA.json, EXAMPLE_EXCHANGE_MANIFEST.json, EXAMPLE_WEB_REVIEW_REQUEST.json, and EXAMPLE_WEB_RESPONSE.json
source_authority.role: Current data-contract definitions and evidence of one completed operational exchange
allowed_uses: Assess strengths, omissions, compatibility constraints, status semantics, and validation behavior
Use the examples to distinguish written protocol from demonstrated practice
prohibited_uses: Treating thesis-specific content in the example as relevant product requirements
Assuming an example field is universally correct merely because it appears once

source_authority.source: Current official web documentation and, when necessary, mature primary open-source project documentation
source_authority.role: Evidence for browser-extension, download, storage, messaging, automation, security, and ChatGPT product constraints
allowed_uses: Verify time-sensitive technical constraints and support architecture decisions
Identify what is robust, brittle, prohibited, or user-mediated in current platforms
prohibited_uses: Inventing undocumented ChatGPT APIs or capabilities
Using marketing claims as proof of reliability
Allowing external sources to override explicit user requirements

objectives: Verify current Chrome Manifest V3 capabilities and restrictions relevant to user gestures, tabs, downloads, content scripts, storage, native messaging, and local communication
Verify current official OpenAI or ChatGPT constraints relevant to browser interaction, file upload/download, authentication, automation, and acceptable use
Identify mature primary-source patterns for resumable, idempotent, human-in-the-loop browser workflows and robust local orchestration
source_requirements: Prefer official Chrome/Chromium, MDN, W3C, and OpenAI documentation for platform claims
Use mature open-source project documentation or repositories only as corroborative implementation evidence
Record the direct URL, page title, access date, and the exact design claim each source supports
Separate documented facts from architectural inference
Do not cite search-result snippets or unverified summaries

context.current_state: A functioning manual protocol already exists. Codex creates one timestamped exchange with request and response folders plus a manifest; Sina manually uploads request files and returns downloaded outputs; Web returns only a schema-valid JSON attachment and declared artifacts; Codex validates and integrates. No implemented extension or orchestration service is supplied in this package. The active_request object in CHATGPT_WEB_PROTOCOL.json identifies this system-design exchange; the EXAMPLE_* files document the prior completed exchange.
context.desired_state: A productized, human-authorized orchestration system in which Codex remains the durable project manager, ChatGPT Web performs bounded intellectual work, a Chrome extension reduces manual transfer through explicit Go and Done actions, and every call remains traceable, recoverable, validated, and linked to project completion.
context.decision_posture: Recommend a design, but explicitly expose trade-offs, confidence, dependencies, assumptions, and decisions that require Sina's approval. Preserve useful parts of the existing system unless a justified migration is safer.
context.implementation_owner: Codex will independently inspect the returned design, verify load-bearing claims, decide what to adopt, and perform later implementation and testing only after approval.

inputs.purpose: Primary product brief for the upgraded system
Current repository-level universal reasoning gate and operational constraints
Operational example of a completed exchange manifest
Operational example of a submitted request
Operational example of a validated main JSON response
Current file-only delivery instruction used to initiate a Web call

requested_work.action: Reconstruct and audit the current manual Web-call system from the supplied authoritative files and operational example.
requested_work.deliverable: A concise current-state model and prioritized gap analysis relative to the product brief.
acceptance_criteria: Separates documented behavior from inference
Identifies which current elements should be retained, extended, migrated, or retired
Calls out contradictions, ambiguous authority, missing state, weak validation, and reliability risks
Does not confuse incidental thesis content with system requirements

requested_work.action: Develop and compare at least three technically feasible architectures for the upgraded system.
requested_work.deliverable: An explicit decision matrix and one recommended architecture with component boundaries and justified technology choices.
acceptance_criteria: Includes a minimal-extension approach, a local-companion or bridge approach, and at least one credible alternative
Scores reliability, security, maintainability, UI brittleness, portability, effort, testability, and user control
States assumptions and platform constraints with citations
Does not rely on an undocumented private ChatGPT API

requested_work.action: Design the end-to-end user workflow, durable state machine, data model, and compatibility/migration strategy.
requested_work.deliverable: A precise lifecycle from call preparation through validated integration, including every normal and exceptional transition.
acceptance_criteria: Defines state ownership, transition initiator, preconditions, side effects, persisted evidence, retry semantics, and terminal conditions
Handles pause, rejection, revision, duplicate actions, browser restarts, lost tabs, partial downloads, wrong files, stale calls, and concurrent projects
Explains how Go and Done remain explicit user-authorized actions
Preserves existing exchange history and provides a safe migration path

requested_work.action: Design validation, completion tracking, observability, security, privacy, and recovery controls.
requested_work.deliverable: Concrete validation gates, threat model, failure taxonomy, audit-trail requirements, and recovery playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Covers request immutability, hashes, schema checks, artifact accounting, provenance, path safety, secret exclusion, least privilege, and unrelated-page-content protection
Distinguishes call completion, artifact acceptance, integration, and whole-project completion
Defines safe behavior when the Web UI or model output is ambiguous
Avoids presenting an aspiration as an absolute reliability guarantee

requested_work.action: Produce a phased implementation and verification roadmap suitable for Codex to execute after user approval.
requested_work.deliverable: A dependency-ordered roadmap with a smallest coherent first slice, testing strategy, acceptance gates, rollback points, and deferred capabilities.
acceptance_criteria: Each phase has objective, inputs, outputs, dependencies, risks, tests, exit criteria, and rollback approach
The first slice demonstrates end-to-end value without requiring the final full product
Testing includes deterministic unit tests, contract tests, extension tests, local integration tests, failure injection, manual UAT, and regression coverage for the old protocol
Lists unresolved decisions that must be answered before implementation

questions.question: What exactly does the current system already accomplish, and where does it fail to satisfy the upgraded brief?
evaluation_criteria: Clear distinction between missing feature and defective feature
questions.required_evidence: Citations to uploaded filenames and exact fields or sections.

questions.question: Which architecture best balances user control, reliability, security, maintainability, and resistance to ChatGPT Web UI changes?
questions.required_evidence: Decision matrix supported by uploaded requirements and current primary-source web documentation.

questions.question: What should the extension automate, what should the local orchestration layer own, and what must remain a direct user action?
evaluation_criteria: Minimized dependence on fragile DOM automation
questions.required_evidence: Role-boundary table tied to platform constraints and the product brief.

questions.question: What durable state machine and data contracts are required to make calls resumable, idempotent, auditable, and correctly associated?
questions.required_evidence: State-transition specification and proposed persisted records.

questions.question: How can response collection be made reliable without silently collecting unrelated ChatGPT page content or assuming an undocumented API?
evaluation_criteria: Explicit user review and Done action
Safe handling of downloads and partial outputs
questions.required_evidence: Concrete collection workflow, platform citations, and failure/recovery cases.

questions.question: What validation and completion rules prevent incomplete or incorrect model output from being silently accepted?
evaluation_criteria: Separation of produced, collected, accepted, and integrated

questions.question: What are the principal security, privacy, and operational threats, and which controls are mandatory before first use?
evaluation_criteria: Threats specific to extensions, local filesystem access, browser sessions, and AI outputs
questions.required_evidence: Threat model with severity, likelihood, mitigation, detection, and residual risk.

questions.question: What should Codex implement and test first, and what evidence is required before expanding automation?
evaluation_criteria: Safe rollback and preservation of the manual workflow

questions.question: Which consequential product and technical decisions remain unresolved and require Sina's explicit approval?
evaluation_criteria: Default assumptions are not silently converted into requirements
questions.required_evidence: Prioritized decision register with recommended defaults and consequences.

requested_artifacts.purpose: Authoritative candidate design for review by Sina and Codex before implementation
acceptance_criteria: Contains current-state audit, requirements traceability, architecture alternatives and decision matrix, recommended architecture, component contracts, end-to-end sequence, state machine, data model, compatibility/migration, validation pipeline, threat model, failure recovery, observability, and unresolved decisions
Every normative requirement uses clear MUST/SHOULD/MAY wording or an equally unambiguous convention
Clearly labels documented facts, recommendations, assumptions, and open decisions
Includes direct citations for time-sensitive platform claims
Is detailed enough to support an implementation plan without inventing missing architecture

requested_artifacts.purpose: Phased execution and verification roadmap for later Codex implementation
acceptance_criteria: Defines a dependency-ordered sequence beginning with a smallest coherent end-to-end slice
For every phase lists scope, deliverables, affected components, prerequisites, risks, automated tests, manual tests, acceptance evidence, rollback, and deferred work
Includes a test matrix for normal operation and failure injection
Preserves the working manual protocol as a fallback until replacement behavior is proven
Does not falsely claim implementation has occurred

stop_condition: Stop only after every uploaded file has been read completely; all W1-W5 work items and Q1-Q9 questions are fully accounted for; current platform claims have been researched and cited; both required artifacts are created as real downloadable files; and the main JSON validates against WEB_RESPONSE_SCHEMA.json and accurately lists every attachment. If any requirement cannot be completed, return only the schema-valid main JSON with status PARTIAL or BLOCKED and record the precise limitation; do not emit chat text.
